one_liner: Incremental-reading PWA: feeds/URLs/PDFs become markdown, Nemotron proposes extracts and drafts notes, you approve, and notes become FSRS-scheduled questions.
problem: People read a lot from feeds and PDFs but retain little; spaced repetition tools require hand-authoring cards.
target_user: Students and self-learners who read RSS/PDFs and want durable recall without writing flashcards.
stack: OpenAI SDK -> NVIDIA NIM / DigitalOcean failover
core_loop: Add URL/PDF/RSS -> ingest to markdown -> Nemotron proposes extracts (pending) -> /read triage screen drafts note + 3 cards per extract -> human approves/edits -> activities scheduled by FSRS -> /review session grades -> review_event hypertable feeds notebook diagnostics; Snowflake writes weekly report.
mocked_or_hardcoded: AI_MOCK=1 default returns committed JSON fixtures; in-memory seed store when DATABASE_URL unset. Live path exists (NVIDIA -> DO failover, guided-JSON downgrade, repair retry). package.json references scripts/benchmark-nemotron.ts which is not in the repo; no eval results committed. Brev NIM handoff doc says the self-hosted model server was never validated.
demo_risks: Live Nemotron depends on NVIDIA API Catalog rate limits or an unvalidated Brev NIM; 45s AI budget per route; PDF upload on Vercel needs Spaces. Mock mode is a safe fallback but then the AI is fixtures.
ui_experience: Polished shadcn/Tailwind app: notebooks with covers and color themes, library with trash/undo, split-pane reader with PDF viewer and Tiptap editor, triage cards, keyboard-driven review session with FSRS intervals, pie-chart diagnostics, theme editor, installable PWA with offline page.
integrity_flags: All 100 commits within Sept 19 10:58 to Sept 20 07:28. README states concepts reused from the team's own MIT obsidian-incremental-reading plugin; no copied-file headers found in tree. No secrets committed (.env.example only). Several commits titled 'claude one shot ...' and 'grok ... fixed it', i.e. heavy AI-assisted coding.
ai_scaffolding_flags: CLAUDE.md (points to AGENTS.md, Next.js auto-generated), 49KB PLAN.md, two large sponsor API briefs (38KB + 48KB), agent handoff docs. Docs ~3.2k lines vs ~22k lines of app code, so docs are not larger than code.
novelty_notes: Spaced repetition and RSS readers are common; the twist is the auto-distill pipeline where the model proposes extracts/notes/cards and the human only approves, with notes as the editable pivot. Nemotron plays a generation role, not chat.
need_notes: Plausible, generic learning-retention need; no user evidence or data beyond the pitch.
wow_moment: Paste a URL, watch extracts appear in the read queue with a drafted note and three questions, approve one, and immediately get quizzed on it under a compressed FSRS clock.
score_rationale: Big, well-engineered build: full ingest-to-review loop, 16 test files, migrations, failover AI client, fixture mode. Category (flashcards/reader) is familiar so novelty is mid. Nemotron role is genuinely non-chat but no eval/benchmark is committed, and the NIM deployment was never validated, capping track fit. UI is attractive but standard web.
judge_summary: A serious, near-production incremental-reading app where Nemotron drafts extracts, notes and quiz cards for you to approve, then FSRS schedules review. Very complete and polished for 24 hours, but a familiar category and the live model path may fall back to fixtures on stage.

target_user: Oversight reviewers, defense counsel, or departments auditing interrogations; explicitly not a legal decision-maker.
stack: ElevenLabs Scribe v2 STT + Flash v2.5 TTS
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning via chat completions
core_loop: Two mics (officer/suspect) -> ~1.3s silence finalizes a turn -> POST /api/audio/transcribe (ElevenLabs or mock) -> POST /api/analyze (mock heuristic | Nemotron classifier + local regex classifier with exact-evidence and speaker validation) -> new concern_id triggers TTS alert + rights reminder -> transcript/concern list -> Save to archive with JSON/CSV export.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Mock mode is the documented demo default (MOCK_STT_TEXT fixed transcript, keyword mock analysis, synthesized chime). Live ElevenLabs and NVIDIA adapters exist with real error taxonomy. Separate 'Interface and Intergration' Streamlit app is heuristic-only and NotImplemented for the Nemotron URL. scripts/run_real_evaluation.py and real_model_cases.json exist but no results are committed.
demo_risks: If run in mock mode every recording yields the same canned line; live mode depends on ElevenLabs STT latency and NVIDIA availability (1s connect/2s read timeouts, then local classifier). Two physical mics and echo suppression in a noisy judging hall.
ui_experience: Custom dark workspace with side nav (Home / Live Monitor / Archives), mic device pickers with live level meters, session timer, transcript list, concern cards with quotes, spoken alerts, save dialog and searchable archive with exports. Functional and clean, not flashy.
integrity_flags: 33 commits, all Sept 19 09:43 to 22:20 (nothing on Sept 20). Several throwaway git-practice files still in root. novelty_notes: Real-time coercion detection during interrogations is an arena hackathon judges rarely see; evidence-linked, exact-quote validation is a thoughtful mechanism.

wow_moment: Judge says 'if you confess I can get you home tonight' into the officer mic and within seconds a voice interrupts: 'Potential inducement detected... You have the right to remain silent.'

demo_risks: Requires Tectonic, Tesseract and a Brev port-forward to a self-hosted vLLM on the demo laptop; 180s LLM timeout; iPad path needs a tunnel URL. If the model or LaTeX fails the app quietly serves the stub.

wow_moment: Photograph a handwritten sheet and the same template reappears with your scrawl typed in teal in the right blanks.

judge_summary: A one-person Tkinter Monte Carlo VaR calculator with correlated paths and a backtest tab. Works, explains itself, no AI, but a familiar textbook project with a plain desktop UI.

target_user: Card-issuer fraud analysts and the developers who tune the ruleset.
stack: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B via chat completions (fetch)
Anthropic Claude Sonnet for rule editing (CLI only)
SVG world map from country GeoJSON
core_loop: Upload .json (+optional notes) -> schema scrub against credit-card-transaction.schema.json -> assemble ruleset files 1-8 + notes + JSON -> POST /api/analyze -> Nemotron (thinking off, JSON only) -> parse/repair (retry once) -> FILE 8 decision -> fraudometer needle sweep, decision card, tabs: Modify Input, Recommendation, Transaction Map (origin->destination arrows), Enterprise Dashboard (history donuts, 3D rule grid). Dev loop: Nemotron generates adversarial cases -> second Nemotron scores -> Claude appends learned lines to RULES 3-7.

one_liner: A live SUMO digital twin of Oakland, Pittsburgh (and a 3x3 grid) where a camera-detected crash triggers candidate responses that are simulated in parallel branches before an agent (Nemotron, Claude or a rule-based mock) recommends, applies and learns from one.
problem: Traffic operators respond to incidents by guesswork; signal retiming, EMS green corridors and diversions should be tested in simulation before being pushed to the street.
target_user: City traffic operations centers / incident managers (NVIDIA Smart City blueprint audience).
stack: Nemotron via NIM chat completions with tool calling
core_loop: SUMO runs a live city streamed over WebSocket -> inject collision (or scripted crash via mock Smart City feed) -> Analyze Response snapshots the twin and runs up to 9 candidate plans (signal timing, EMS corridor, diversion) as parallel SUMO branches vs baseline -> KPI comparison, safety validator rejects unsafe plan -> recommendation -> autonomous episode: analyst (mock/Claude/Nemotron as MCP tool-caller) applies plan to live twin, monitors, scorecards, stores a lesson for the next crash.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Rule-based mock agent and mock Smart City feed are the only paths ever run; README states 24 times that things are 'not run'/'not verified', including all Claude and Nemotron inference, VSS client, Cloud Run deploy, map switching and the operator flow. Mock episode completed once in a smoke test. Traffic demand and signal timing are synthetic. Frontend has a ?fixture=scenario replay mode. Dependency 'httpx2' could not be verified here.
demo_risks: Nemotron tool-calling loop is untested against NIM (tool result truncation at 16k chars noted in TOOL_TODO_FIX.txt, schema $ref/anyOf concerns, uncaught exceptions); SUMO at 4x-16x on a laptop; MCP over Cloud Run returns 421. Safe demo is the mock analyst, which is not AI.
ui_experience: Very polished dark ops console: MapLibre map of real Oakland streets with congestion-colored roads, signal heads, moving vehicles, EMS responder, incident markers, cameras, 'thinking' route overlay, legend; time-scale controls; KPI sparklines; scenario comparison charts; agent/episode panel. Screenshot committed. Judges can inject a crash and watch queues form.

Git starts Sept 19 09:28 (2-line README), brainstorm at 09:59, then one 87-file, 10,270-line 'milestone 1' commit at 12:12, about one hour after hacking start; either pre-hackathon preparation or bulk agent generation, and the repo alone cannot distinguish. All 111 commits are Sept 19-20. No secrets committed.
ai_scaffolding_flags: Heavy: 18KB CLAUDE.md with a hard rule that agents never run tests, .claude/launch.json, copilot-swe-agent[bot] commits, 'codex/' branches, milestone MASTER/handoff docs, TOOL_TODO_FIX.txt referring to 'agent B' and 'agent D'. README is 96KB (~1,300 lines); docs total ~4.9k lines vs ~16k lines of code, so docs are large but not larger than code.
novelty_notes: Simulation-in-the-loop incident response with parallel SUMO branches exposed as MCP tools, plus a learning episode with stored lessons, is an uncommon and genuinely new mechanism at a student hackathon; the real Oakland map makes it local.
